Acquisition / Email delivery and engagement

Outbound email bounce rate

The percentage of attempted campaign recipient-message pairs classified as bounced after the agreed delivery window. Hard bounces and final soft bounces count once; retries do not create additional recipients.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The percentage of attempted campaign recipient-message pairs classified as bounced after the agreed delivery window. Hard bounces and final soft bounces count once; retries do not create additional recipients.

%

How we use it

We examine list hygiene, recipient validity, sending infrastructure, and provider responses before expanding outreach volume.

Transparent calculationUnique bounced recipient-message pairs / unique attempted recipient-message pairs in the same send cohort * 100
bounced recipient messages80
attempted recipient messages4,000

80 / 4,000 * 100 = 2% outbound delivery bounce.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Sending mailbox and provider
  • List source and verification date
  • Hard versus final soft bounce

Questions we investigate

  • Which list source creates repeated failures?
  • Are soft bounces temporary or persistent?
  • Did provider blocks increase after a volume change?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Verify addresses and suppress invalid recipients.
  • Inspect delivery codes and sending configuration.
  • Review volume and retries against provider policies.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Deliverability lead
Daily during launches; weekly for established sends.

Required data

  • Unique campaign recipient-message IDs
  • Attempt and final bounce timestamps
  • Delivery codes and suppression history

Read the measure with context

Zero attempts makes the rate undefined. This is an email delivery measure, not website bounce rate. Final soft-bounce treatment depends on the cutoff; suppressed contacts never attempted are outside this denominator.
